cells.why: install size figure stale (~256 MB → ~280 MiB); 2.1.311 startup trims
cells.new: 🟡 Heavy install (~280 MiB binary); `--bare` / `--safe-mode` trim startup; no published startup benchmarks
cells.detail: 🟡 — The 2.1.311 binary is ~280 MiB. Measured locally: `claude --version` ≈10 ms, 36 MB RSS (fast path only, not a full session start). `--bare` skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync, attribution, auto-memory, background prefetches, keychain reads and CLAUDE.md discovery (sets CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1); `--safe-mode` disables customizations. Pro/Max relaunches within an hour of the last check skip two network requests, and launches whose only arguments are options start faster. `/heapdump`; `CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_LIMIT` caps Bash/Monitor memory via cgroup on Linux. — _Evidence:_ local `du -sh ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.311`, `/usr/bin/time claude --version`; help (`--bare`, `--safe-mode`); CL v2.1.311; cc:tools-reference#memory-limit-on-linux-and-wsl

details.cc: ❌ — MCP clients issue `tools/call` and wait for the reply on the turn; nothing moves a slow call to a background task and no task-augmented result (`tasks/get`, `tasks/result`, `taskSupport`) is handled. `/bg` backgrounds agent tasks, not MCP calls. — _Evidence:_ `src/MCP/HttpMcpServer.php:360`, `src/MCP/SseMcpServer.php:271`, `src/ClaudeCodeMcpClient.php:631`; grep for `tasks/get|tasks/result|taskSupport|autoBackground` in `src` finds nothing
details.web: ❌ — The web UI has no MCP client; MCP calls execute server-side and the browser only sees tool events, with no background or task state. — _Evidence:_ web:protocol/generated.ts (no MCP task events); `src/MCP/HttpMcpServer.php:360`
details.claude: ✅ — An MCP tool call in the main conversation that is still running after 2 minutes moves to a `/tasks` background task, and its result arrives as a notification (`CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS`; off in `-p` unless `CLAUDE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1`). A server on protocol revision 2026-07-28 can answer `tools/call` with an MCP task (tasks extension). The footer counts running tasks, and Claude Code polls their status. A remote task keeps running after exit and is followed again on resume; `x` in `/tasks` asks the server to cancel. MCP tasks are a public beta in the CLI, Agent SDK and GitHub Actions from v2.1.304, and are not available in VS Code or the desktop app. — _Evidence:_ cc:mcp#automatic-backgrounding-of-long-tool-calls; cc:mcp#mcp-tasks-that-run-on-the-server; cc:mcp#mcp-tasks-for-server-authors; cc:env-vars (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND`, v2.1.304)

new_rows.feature: 🆕 Deep links (URL opens a local session in a given directory with a pre-filled, unsent prompt)

cells.cc: ❌ No URL-scheme handler; a session starts only from the CLI or TUI
cells.web: 🟡 Hash routes (`/#/s/:id`) link to an existing session; no URL carries a directory or a pre-filled prompt
cells.claude: ✅ `claude-cli://` links open a local terminal session in the linked directory with the prompt pre-filled, never auto-sent

details.cc: ❌ — No OS URL-scheme registration or handler exists; sessions start from `candy-code` arguments or the TUI. — _Evidence:_ grep for `x-scheme-handler`, `registerProtocol`, a custom URL scheme in `src`, `bin`, `docs` finds nothing
details.web: 🟡 — The router uses hash history so `/#/s/:id` opens an existing session and `/#code=` carries the sign-in code. No route starts a session in a chosen directory or pre-fills the composer. — _Evidence:_ web:router.ts:10-25
details.claude: ✅ — Claude Code registers the `claude-cli://` scheme with the OS. A link carries a working directory and prompt text, and opens a new terminal window running Claude Code there with the prompt typed but not sent. A `Prompt from an external link` warning stays below the input, with a length warning past 1,000 chars. Permission rules, CLAUDE.md and trust prompts apply as usual. The feature is meant for runbooks, alerts, dashboards and READMEs, and handler registration can be managed or disabled per platform. — _Evidence:_ cc:deep-links

new_rows.feature: 🆕 Contextual plugin recommendations (install suggestions triggered by repo/files/commands or by a tool's hint)

cells.cc: ❌ Plugin bundles are discovered from disk only; no install suggestions from session signals or tool hints
cells.web: ❌ No plugin discovery or recommendation surface
cells.claude: ✅ Marketplace `relevance` signals (dirs, files read, commands run) and CLI `<claude-code-hint />` tags trigger install suggestions

details.cc: ❌ — `BundleDiscovery` loads installed `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` bundles; there is no marketplace, `relevance` block or `<claude-code-hint />` parsing, so nothing suggests a plugin. — _Evidence:_ `src/Bundles/BundleDiscovery.php`, `src/Bundles/Bundle.php:29`; grep for `claude-code-hint` and plugin `relevance` in `src` finds nothing
details.web: ❌ — The web UI has no plugin install or recommendation surface. — _Evidence:_ grep for `claude-code-hint|relevance` in web:src-web finds nothing
details.claude: ✅ — A marketplace entry's `relevance` block (working directory, files Claude read, commands it ran) makes Claude Code suggest installing that plugin when a session matches, once an admin allowlists the marketplace in managed settings. A third-party CLI or SDK can print a one-line `<claude-code-hint />` tag to stderr; Claude Code strips it from Bash/PowerShell output before the model sees it and shows a one-time install prompt for that tool's official-marketplace plugin. The LSP recommendation dialog offers code-intelligence plugins when a server binary is on PATH. — _Evidence:_ cc:plugins/relevance; cc:plugins/cli-hints; cc:plugins/code-intelligence

new_rows.feature: 🆕 Usage-optimisation advice (usage attributed to skills/subagents/plugins/MCP servers, with one-step fixes)

cells.cc: ❌ `/usage 7/30/all` gives day x model rollups only; no per-skill/agent/MCP attribution or recommendations
cells.web: ❌ Status bar shows session spend only; no attribution or recommendations
cells.claude: ✅ `/usage` attributes plan usage to skills, subagents, plugins, MCP servers and recommends fixes (`f` applies); `/skill-doctor`

details.cc: ❌ — `/usage` folds the `usage_records` ledger by day and model (windows 7, 30, all). It does not attribute spend to skills, subagents, plugins or MCP servers, lists no heavy loops and offers no applicable fixes. — _Evidence:_ `src/Host/Commands/UsageHostCommand.php:30-60`, `builtin-commands/2210-usage.php`
details.web: ❌ — The web shows running spend and per-turn cost in the status bar and session tiles, with no breakdown by skill, agent or MCP server and no advice. — _Evidence:_ web:components/StatusBar.vue:68, web:components/grid/SessionTile.vue
details.claude: ✅ — On Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise, `/usage` attributes the last 24 h or 7 days of usage to skills, subagents, plugins and individual MCP servers. It lists the heaviest loops and recommends changes, one row each with its usage share (e.g. trimming a 49K-token CLAUDE.md). `f` applies what it can (v2.1.305+): it runs any `/effort` rows, then has Claude make the rest, showing each change first. The same recommendations appear in VS Code and `/doctor`. `/skill-doctor` reports each skill's context cost and use and where to turn unused ones off. — _Evidence:_ cc:costs#plan-usage-breakdown; cc:costs#apply-recommendations-with-the-fix-shortcut; cc:skills#find-unused-skills; cc:commands (`/skill-doctor`); CL v2.1.305
